items.title: A problem with a shared workspace
items.prompt: You use a shared study room in your residence hall. Recently, the room has been left untidy and some students have had difficulty finding a seat. Write an email to the residence coordinator, Ms. Patel. Explain the problem, describe how it affects students, and suggest a practical solution. You have 7 minutes for this practice task.
checklist: I explain both the untidiness and seating problem.
I describe a specific effect on students.
I propose a practical solution and make a polite request.
My greeting, tone and closing suit the coordinator.
My ideas are clear, connected and grammatically controlled.
items.sample:
Dear Ms. Patel,
I am writing about the shared study room on the second floor. Over the past week, food wrappers and unused books have often been left on the tables. These items make it difficult to tell which seats are available. Yesterday, several students returned to their rooms without finding a place to study.
Could we introduce a simple rule asking students to clear their tables before leaving? A notice at the entrance and a small bin beside the door might help. It could also be useful to remind residents that belongings should not be left to reserve a seat for a long period.
Thank you for considering these suggestions.
Best regards,
Alex

items.title: Campus tour · sentence 1
items.prompt: You are listening to information during a campus tour. Listen to the sentence, then repeat it as accurately and clearly as you can.
items.script: The help desk is beside the main entrance.
checklist: I repeat all the words in the original order.
I keep a natural rhythm and place pauses at meaningful boundaries.
